hesternal tense, past day tense, for things that happened yesterday.
perfective aspect, a completed action taken as a whole.
imperfective aspect, an incomplete action in process.
frequentative aspect, indicates the verb happens multiple times, for example bite frequentative_aspect is equivalent to chewing.
potential mood, something that is probable according to the speaker.
jussive mood, for remote commands that are to be conveyed to another recipient.
dubitative mood, for saying things the speaker is doubtful of, as for expressing sarcasm.
benedictive mood, for expressing blessings.
declarative mood, for declaring the begining of a program or essay.
realis mood, for declaring something, the most common kind of sentence.
epistemic mood, to indicate that something is possible.
deontic mood, to indicate what should be different.
imperative mood, to indicate direct commands.
directive-mood, indicates how to perform an action.
desiderative mood, to indicate what the speaker wants to happen.
imprecative mood, for uttering curses.
hortative mood, for pleading or begging.
interrogative mood, for questions.
precative mood, for requests.
conditional mood, for if then statements. The if clause comes before the `cu' the then clause comes after.
habitual aspect, something that happens habitualy.
gnomic aspect, for expressing a general truth.
gnomic mood, for expressing an axiom.
hodiernal tense, for expressing today.
crastinal tense, for expressing tomorrow.
telic aspect, for actions that have a definite end point. finite or limited.
atelic aspect, for actions that have no particular end point. infinte or unlimited.
cessative aspect, for referring to the end of an action, when it is ceasing. inchoative_aspect_ is begining
momentane aspect, for referring to momentary actions, like the unfurling of flower petals in the morning
delimitive aspect, for referring to events of limited duration, like a limited time offer
inchoative aspect, for expressing the begining of a state or action
semelfactive aspect, for expressing a sudden quick event, like a blink or a sneeze.
speculative mood, for expressing speculation, hypothesis, ``could be''
prohibitive mood, for expressing something is not allowed, inverse of permissive_mood_, potential response to admonitive mood
permissive mood, for granting permission to do something, potential response to admonitive mood.
deliberative mood, asking if speaker should do something.
retrospective aspect, the event happened prior to other things being discussed.
continuative aspect, the state is continuing to occur, it is `still' occuring.
progressive aspect, the action is in progress, it is happening actively.
prospective aspect, the event happens after the other things under consideration.
commissive mood, for making promises, commitments
optatative mood, for expressing wishes or hopes.
admonitive mood, a request for permission to do something.
apprehensive mood, for expressing fears or warnings.
successive clause, for putting several sentences in a sequence, similar to this happened, then that happened
dependent clause, similar in usage to `that', a sentence that is within another sentence
propositive mood, for making proposals or offers, let's
vocative case, the intended recipient of the sentence. for example `O' in `O god, hear my prayers.' discourse_context destination_case
topic case, the topic about which the sentence is. `regarding topic, some sentence.''. discourse_context way_case
associative case, indicates the noun phrase is an associated group of the agent. social_context location_case.
comitative case, indicates the noun phrase is accompanying the other actors of the sentence. social_context way_case.
benefactive case, indicates the noun phrase is the benficiary of the sentence. social_context destination_case.
pegative case, indicates motion from a person. social_context source_case.
instrumental case, indicates the method or tool used. person_context_way_case.
adessive case, indicates personal location. person_context location_case.
causal case, indicates the noun phrase is the cause. person_context source_case.
adpositional case, indicates preceding stem is the case for this noun phrase.
source case, indicates a source noun phrase, from. is used for constructing complex cases or by itself.
essive case, indicates a duration of time at which the noun phrase occurs. time_context way_case.
temporal case, indicates a specific time. time_context location_case.
initiative case, indicates the begining of an action. time_context source_case
terminative case, indicates temporal destination or goal. time_context destination_case.
evitative case, indicates the noun phrase happened before the rest of the sentence. time_context retrospective_aspect
antessive case, indicates the noun phrase precedes the rest of the sentence. space_context retrospective_aspect
ablative case, indicates a source noun phrase, from. is used as a standalone case. space_context source_case
perlative case, indicates motion through space. space_context way_case.
locative case, indicates location in space. space_context location_case.
lative case, indicates spatial motion towards the noun phrase. space_context destination_case.
dative case, indicates motion towards the noun phrase. destination_case.
vialis case, indicates motion through the noun phrase. used a standalone case. way_case.
quotative case, indicates a quote. discource_context location_case.
distributive case, indicates for-each the noun phrase, or per the noun phrase. iterative for loops.
evidential case, for citing a source as evidence. discource_context source_case
multiplicative case, for indicating how many times the event occurs. as for frequentative_aspect or simple repeat loops.
sublative case, indicates motion toward the underside of nounphrase. under_context destination_case.
subessive case, indicates location at the underside of nounphrase. under_context location_case.
oblique case, indicates intersection with noun phrase, such as an orbit or street that is being crossed at an oblique angle.
evitative case, indicates that the noun phrase is feared or avoided.
delative case, indicates motion away from noun phrase. surface_context source_case.
allative case, indicates motion onto a surface. surface_context destination_case.
prosecutive case, indicates motion along a surface. surface_context way_case.
superlative case, indicates motion above a surface. surface_context way_case.
superessive case, indicates location on a surface. surface_context location_case.
superessive case, indicates location on a surface. surface_context location_case.
partitive case, a subcase that indicates only partial usage of the noun phrase. lazy argument loading.
elative case, indicates motion `out of' some noun phrase. interior_context source_case.
ilative case, indicates motion `into' some noun phrase. interior_context destination_case.
prolative case, indicates motion via an interior. interior_context way_case.
inessive case, indicates the noun phrase being in at. interior_context location_case.
centric case, indicates the noun phrase being the centre. Such as a star or actor.
exocentric case, indicates the noun phrase orbiting the other participants. Such as a moon or audience.
abessive case, indicating the absence of the noun phrase referred to object. state_context negatory_quantifier
excessive case, indicates motion from a state. state_context source_case.
modal case, indicates the ability or probability of the sentence. state_context location_case. neural weight.
agentive case, the agent of a transitive verb.
intransitive case, the subject of an intransitive verb.
intransitive case, the subject of an intransitive verb.
patient case, the object of a transitive verb.
existential clause, for asserting something that can be imagined.
